claim: The Internet Archive's Wayback Machine has archived over 835 billion web pages since 1996 — preserving the history of the ephemeral web.
corrected_claim: As of October 2025, the Wayback Machine had archived more than 1 trillion web pages, with the Internet Archive capturing pages since at least 1995.

claim: Toxoplasma gondii infects 30-50% of humans — possibly altering behavior and risk-taking.

claim: The deepest snowfall ever recorded was 11.82 meters (38.8 feet) on Mount Ibuki, Japan, on February 14, 1927.
quote: Deepest snowfall recorded: 11.82 meters (38.8 ft) on ... Mount Ibuki, Japan on 14 February 1927.

claim: Phosphorene (2D black phosphorus) is a semiconductor with a tunable bandgap, unlike graphene which has none, making it promising for electronics.
corrected_claim: Phosphorene is a competitor to graphene because it has a nonzero band gap that can be tuned by strain and layer number — from 0.3 eV in bulk to 1.88 eV in a monolayer.

note: Page does not explicitly say graphene has no band gap

claim: The Rosetta Code wiki documents solutions to programming tasks in hundreds of languages — revealing both similarities and fascinating differences between languages.

claim: Toxoplasma can only sexually reproduce in cats — all other hosts are 'dead ends' for its lifecycle.
corrected_claim: Toxoplasma can sexually reproduce only within the intestines of members of the cat family; in all other hosts it reproduces only asexually, making them intermediate hosts.
quote: can sexually reproduce only within the intestines of members of the cat family ... All other hosts – in which only asexual reproduction can occur – are intermediate hosts.
note: Other hosts are intermediate hosts, not 'dead ends'.

claim: Mount Baker, Washington, received 29.0 meters (95 feet) of snow in a single season (1998-1999), the world record for seasonal snowfall.
quote: Most in one season (1 July – 30 June): 29.0 meters, (95 ft); ... Mount Baker, Washington, United States, 1998 through 1999.

claim: Silicene, stanene, and germanene are 2D materials made from silicon, tin, and germanium respectively, each with unique properties beyond graphene.
corrected_claim: Silicene, a 2D form of silicon, is not flat like graphene but periodically buckled — which gives it a band gap tuneable by an external electric field.

claim: Code golf is competitive programming where the shortest source code wins — APL and J programs often win due to their terse syntax.

note: Page does not say APL and J programs often win

claim: Giardia lamblia has two nuclei per cell — giving it a 'face-like' appearance under microscopy.

claim: Marble Bar, Australia, experienced 160 consecutive days above 37.8°C (100°F) from October 1923 to April 1924.
quote: Marble Bar, Western Australia | 31 October 1923 to 7 April 1924 (160 days)
note: Record: most consecutive days above 37.8 °C (100 °F).

claim: Topological insulators conduct electricity only on their surfaces while being insulators in the bulk, potentially revolutionizing spintronics and quantum computing.
quote: A topological insulator is a material whose interior behaves as an electrical insulator while its surface behaves as an electrical conductor ... The most promising applications of topological insulators are spintronic devices and dissipationless transistors for quantum computers

claim: The International Obfuscated C Code Contest (IOCCC) has celebrated creative abuse of the C language since 1984 — winning entries are deliberately unreadable.

claim: Cryptosporidium survives chlorination of swimming pools — the leading cause of recreational water illness.

note: Page does not call it the leading cause of recreational water illness

corrected_claim: In Weyl semimetals, electrons behave as a solid-state analogue of relativistic massless particles, and the high mobility of these Weyl fermions may find use in electronics and computing.

note: 'Ultra-high-speed devices' goes beyond the page's 'may find use in electronics and computing'

claim: Quines are programs that output their own source code without reading themselves — they exist in virtually every programming language.

claim: Entamoeba histolytica causes amebic dysentery — the third leading parasitic cause of death worldwide.

claim: The fastest wind speed in a tornado was calculated at 516.6 km/h (321 mph) during the 1999 Bridge Creek-Moore tornado in Oklahoma.

claim: Acanthamoeba keratitis comes from contaminated contact lens solutions — blindness from protozoa.

claim: Debian has been reproduced bit-for-bit from source code — reproducible builds prevent supply chain attacks by making binaries verifiable.
